text:
Alex Rivera: quick sync — I'm proposing a single fleet log envelope + sampling/redaction canary for GPU pods in us-west1. want to land a schema that all downstream systems (prom/grafana/log-pipeline) can validate. can we get alignment today?
Priya Shah: can you drop the proposed schema snippet here? easier to comment inline.
Alex Rivera: sure — rough idea below (fields minimal to start):
```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "ts": "2026-03-18T14:31:00Z",
  "cluster": "gpu-pool-1",
  "region": "us-west1",
  "pod": "pod-xyz",
  "job_type": "infer",
  "request_id": "<uuid>",
  "meta": {"model": "redwood-7b", "seq_len": 512},
  "payload": {"kind": "trace|sample|metric", "body": "<redacted-or-hash>"}
}
```
Marcos Li: +1 to v and request_id. we should include a short list of legacy keys mapping so the pipeline can hot-map old logs -> new schema (avoid dashboard breakage).
Jen O'Neill: critical: dashboards use `region` and `job_type` tags. please keep them. also add `ingest_version` label for k8s prom relabel.
Tom Becker: a heads up on cost: if we log full prompt bodies at 100%, Kinesis/ingest costs jump ~20% based on last quarter numbers. sampling + redaction needed.
Alex Rivera: agreed. proposed sampling rules: 1) default sample rate for user prompts = 1% (random), 2) always sample errors and SLO breaches 100%, 3) increase to 5% when model_latency > 2x p95 for 5m window, 4) dedicated customers can opt-in to higher retention via account flag.
Priya Shah: for PII, we should never send raw prompts unless opt-in. plan: pseudonymize tokens + store hash prefix for de-dupe. redaction library will emit `payload.body: <redacted>` or `payload.body_hash: sha256:<prefix>`. also add `redaction_version` field.
Marcos Li: edge case: some training/debug jobs need full payloads. add `data_access: full` label guarded by a signed consent token; route those logs to a separate INGRESS that requires dedicated contract. don't mix with normal pipeline.
Jen O'Neill: validation/monitoring checklist for canary:
- panel: schema_validation.count (per region)
- panel: redaction.failures (logs that failed redaction)
- panel: sampling.effective_rate (observed vs configured)
- alert: schema_validation.rate > 0.1% for 10m -> paging to eng-sre
- alert: redaction.failures > 5 for 5m -> ops channel
Alex Rivera: ops: can we add a JSON schema lint job that runs in CI on the pipeline repo? quick pre-deploy gate.
ops-bot: [ops-bot] created pipeline-ci job: `log-schema-lint` (will run on PRs to infra/logging).
Tom Becker: also add cost delta estimate dashboard: ingest_bytes_by_schema_version. that way product folks can see delta.
Priya Shah: can we do a canary rollout plan? my suggestion:
- canary window: 48h in us-west1 on GPU pool tagged `canary-logs` (5% of pods)
- monitor schema_validation + redaction.failures + ingest_bytes
- if metrics stable -> promote to 25% -> 7 days -> full roll
Marcos Li: make sure we have a rollback `redaction_mode=passthrough` toggle defaulting to safe. also ensure kibana/log-explorer can still parse old keys when both v=1 and legacy present.
Jen O'Neill: note on alert tuning: schema_validation flapping often because of tail errors. set alert threshold to 0.1% not absolute counts. we should avoid noisy pages.
Alex Rivera: ops-bot, kick the canary in us-west1 tomorrow 09:00 PT if nobody objects. add the canary playbook and runbook to the ticket.
ops-bot: [ops-bot] canary deploy scheduled: `log-schema-canary` -> us-west1 @ 2026-03-19T16:00:00Z (pods: 200 total, 10 canary).
Priya Shah: quick approval from me. +1 on pseudonymization approach.
Tom Becker: +1 from infra/cost side as long as we have the ingest dashboard and rollback.
Marcos Li: +1 if we get the legacy mapping and a `data_access` separation.
Jen O'Neill: +1 — will follow up with Grafana panels PR.
Alex Rivera: thanks all — i'll open the RFC PR with schema + sampling config + runbook. plan to merge after 24h review unless objections. :thumbsup:
